s1.syndrome_frame: Rectal ulcer with a history of radiation therapy
salient_findings: Large deep-cratered solitary ulcer on the anterior rectal wall
key_facts: 57-year-old man
Asymptomatic
History of stage IIIc localized prostate cancer
Completed a course of prostate-directed radiation therapy with a SpaceOAR hydrogel spacer
Mild straining with bowel movements
Occasional passage of mucus
Large deep-cratered solitary ulcer on the anterior rectal wall
Firm margins, friability, and exudate
Biopsies of the lesion were negative for malignancy
Normal appearance of remainder of rectum without radiation-induced changes

raw.rationale: The patient's history of prostate-directed radiation therapy and the presence of a large deep-cratered solitary ulcer on the anterior rectal wall with firm margins, friability, and exudate, along with biopsies negative for malignancy, support this diagnosis. The normal appearance of the remainder of the rectum without radiation-induced changes also points towards a localized effect of radiation.

rejected.label: Radiation proctitis
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of radiation therapy, radiation proctitis typically presents with more diffuse inflammation and damage to the rectal mucosa, which is not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Solitary rectal ulcer syndrome
rejected.why: This condition is usually associated with symptoms of constipation, straining, and rectal prolapse, which are not prominent in this patient's history.

rejected.label: Rectal adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: Biopsies of the lesion were negative for malignancy, ruling out rectal adenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Prostate cancer metastasis
rejected.why: The biopsies were negative for malignancy, and there's no indication of metastatic disease in the provided information.
